summary: Implemented ProvisioningToolsViewModel, ProvisioningToolsView.axaml + codebehind, and ProvisioningToolsViewModelTests. ViewModel uses CommunityToolkit.Mvvm (ObservableObject, [ObservableProperty], [RelayCommand]), exposes Stage/BytesReceived/BytesTotal/Error/IsProvisioning observable properties, RetryCommand (CanExecute when Error != null && !IsProvisioning), CancelCommand, ProvideManuallyCommand (stub for WP-010), and StartAsync() entry point. A private SyncProgress<T> inner class is used for IProgress<T> to ensure synchronous callback dispatch (predictable in tests; Avalonia handles cross-thread PropertyChanged). View uses compiled x:DataType bindings with StringConverters.IsNotNullOrEmpty for conditional visibility. All 5 acceptance criteria verified. 39/39 App.Tests pass (5 new); 42/42 VideoIndexer.Tests pass; 55/55 Infrastructure.Tests pass. Build: 0 errors, 0 warnings.

comments.note: ProvisioningToolsViewModel uses a private SyncProgress<T> inner class (synchronous IProgress<T> dispatch) instead of the standard Progress<T>. This avoids the ThreadPool-scheduling lag in tests but relies on Avalonia 11's tolerance of cross-thread PropertyChanged notifications. A future refactor could make the dispatcher injectable (e.g., IDispatcher abstraction) for environments that require explicit UI-thread marshaling.
ProvideManuallyCommand is a no-op stub in ProvisioningToolsViewModel.cs — acknowledged as out of scope for WP-009 per spec, deferred to WP-010 (file-picker wiring).

ProgressBar in ProvisioningToolsView.axaml uses computed double properties (ProgressValue, ProgressMaximum) on the ViewModel to avoid Avalonia compiled-binding type mismatch between long/long? and double. This is correct and clean, though it adds a small amount of boilerplate to the VM.

comments.note: ProvideManuallyCommand is a documented no-op stub pending WP-010. The Retry and ProvideManually buttons are correctly hidden until Error is non-null (IsVisible binding via StringConverters.IsNotNullOrEmpty). The Cancel button is always visible.

After CancelCommand, Stage='Cancelled' and Error=null so RetryCommand.CanExecute=false. Users cannot retry a cancelled provisioning attempt without a fresh navigation. This may be a UX concern if users need to retry after accidental cancellation.

SyncProgress<T> inner class dispatches progress callbacks on the provisioner's thread. Avalonia handles cross-thread PropertyChanged, which is correct for Avalonia 11, but relies on Avalonia's threading model. If the provisioner runs on a thread pool thread, UI updates are deferred to Avalonia's dispatcher implicitly.

summary: Code review passed. ProvisioningToolsViewModel is clean, idiomatic CommunityToolkit.Mvvm. Compiled AXAML bindings are correct. SyncProgress<T> design is well-reasoned. ConfigureAwait(false) + Avalonia 11 cross-thread PropertyChanged is a documented and valid trade-off. Tests correctly cover all 3 ACs with well-designed fakes. One low-priority IDisposable observation and one documentation-forward item recorded. No blocking issues.

comments.note: ProvisioningToolsViewModel holds a CancellationTokenSource? _cts field but does not implement IDisposable. The previous CTS is correctly disposed at the start of each RunProvisioningAsync call, but the final CTS (after the last provisioning run) is never explicitly disposed. CancellationTokenSource has a finalizer so no permanent resource leak occurs, but implementing IDisposable (disposing _cts in Dispose()) is the standard .NET best practice for classes that own IDisposable fields.

[documentation-forward] ProvisioningToolsViewModel uses ConfigureAwait(false) on EnsureAsync, meaning Stage='Complete' and IsProvisioning=false (in finally) execute on a ThreadPool thread, not the UI thread. This works correctly in Avalonia 11 which handles cross-thread PropertyChanged, but is a non-obvious architectural decision. A class-level <remarks> XML tag documenting this trade-off would prevent future maintainers from adding unnecessary Dispatcher.UIThread.Post wrappers or misdiagnosing threading issues.
